source.text: אַחֲרֵ֨י הַדְּבָרִ֤ים וְהָאֱמֶת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה בָּ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּבֹ֣א בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וַיִּ֨חַן֙ עַל־הֶעָרִ֣ים הַבְּצֻר֔וֹת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְבִקְעָ֥ם אֵלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: After the matters and the faithfulness the these came Sennacherib king of Assyria, and he came into Judah and encamped against the cities the fortified, and he said to break them open for himself.

en.L: After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came, and he came into Judah and encamped against the fortified cities, and he thought to break them open for himself.
en.B: After these faithful deeds, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah. He camped against the fortified cities, intending to break into them and take them for himself.
en.R: Hezekiah had done all these things faithfully. After that, King Sennacherib of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He camped outside the walled cities and planned to break through their walls and take them for himself.

decisions.choice: these things and this faithfulness: these faithful deeds of Hezekiah
decisions.reason: The two nouns are joined and share one "these", so they describe one thing: the acts just told in chapters 29-31, which 31:20-21 sums up as what was good, right and faithful before Yahweh. The writer sets the invasion after Hezekiah's faithfulness, not as a punishment for unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: Sennacherib's invasion, told more briefly than in 2 Kings 18:13
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 18:13 (and Isaiah 36:1) dates the attack to Hezekiah's fourteenth year and says Sennacherib took all the fortified cities. Chronicles gives no date and says only that he camped against them and meant to break into them; it leaves out Hezekiah's surrender and tribute (2 Kings 18:14-16).

decisions.choice: he said to break them open for himself: he intended to break into them and take them
decisions.reason: "Said" here means said to himself, that is, intended or thought. "Break open" is used of breaching a city wall.

decisions.choice: these faithful deeds
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the two joined nouns as one phrase. Readable says in a clause who was faithful.

source.text: וַיַּרְא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּי־בָ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֑יב וּפָנָ֕יו לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Hezekiah that had come Sennacherib, and his face [was] for war against Jerusalem,

en.L: And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and his face [was set] for war against Jerusalem,
en.B: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and was set on making war against Jerusalem,
en.R: Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and meant to attack Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: his face was for war: he was determined to attack
decisions.reason: To set the face toward something is to turn one's purpose to it. Sennacherib's aim was Jerusalem itself, not only the outlying towns.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 3
decisions.reason: Verse 2 gives the occasion; verse 3 tells what Hezekiah did about it.

source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ עִם־שָׂרָיו֙ וְגִבֹּרָ֔יו לִסְתּוֹם֙ אֶת־מֵימֵ֣י הָעֲיָנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִח֣וּץ לָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּעְזְרֽוּהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and he took counsel with his princes and his mighty [men] to stop up the waters of the springs which [were] from outside to the city, and they helped him.

en.L: and he took counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs that [were] outside the city; and they helped him.
en.B: he consulted with his officials and his warriors about stopping the water of the springs outside the city, and they supported him.
en.R: So he talked with his leaders and his best soldiers. They agreed to block off the springs outside the city, and they helped him do it.

decisions.choice: his princes and his mighty men: his court officials and his leading warriors
decisions.reason: *Sarim* are the king's high officials; *gibborim* are proven fighting men. Hezekiah takes advice from both the court and the army.

decisions.choice: stopping the springs outside the city: denying water to a besieging army
decisions.reason: An army camped around a city needed water. By blocking or hiding the springs outside the walls, Hezekiah meant to leave the Assyrians without it (verse 4), while the city kept its own supply (verse 30).

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders; mighty men / warriors / best soldiers
decisions.reason: *Sar* follows the usual table for a king's officials. *Gibborim* is "mighty men" at Literal and is named by what they were at the other levels.

source.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ עַם־רָ֔ב וַֽיִּסְתְּמוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַמַּעְיָנ֔וֹת וְאֶת־הַנַּ֛חַל הַשּׁוֹטֵ֥ף בְּתוֹךְ־הָאָ֖רֶץ לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֤מָּה יָב֨וֹאוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר וּמָצְא֖וּ מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And were gathered people many, and they stopped up all the springs and the wadi the flowing in [the] midst of the land, saying, why should come [the] kings of Assyria and find waters many?

en.L: And many people were gathered, and they stopped up all the springs and the brook that flowed through the midst of the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?"
en.B: A great many people gathered and blocked all the springs and the stream running across the land. "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find water in plenty?" they said.
en.R: Many people came together and blocked all the springs and the stream that ran through the land. They said, "Why should the kings of Assyria come here and find plenty of water?"

decisions.choice: the brook that flowed through the land: probably the stream fed by the Gihon spring in the Kidron Valley
decisions.reason: The text does not name it. The only large spring at Jerusalem was the Gihon, in the valley east of the City of David, and verse 30 tells how Hezekiah stopped its upper outlet. The stream is most likely the overflow from that spring running down the valley.

decisions.choice: the kings of Assyria: the Assyrian king and his forces, or Assyrian kings in general
decisions.reason: The plural may speak of Assyria's kings as a type, since they had come before (28:16, 20), or include the vassal kings who marched with Sennacherib. Either way the danger meant is the present invasion.

source.text: וַיִּתְחַזַּ֡ק וַיִּבֶן֩ אֶת־כָּל־הַחוֹמָ֨ה הַפְּרוּצָ֜ה וַיַּ֣עַל עַל־הַמִּגְדָּל֗וֹת וְלַח֨וּצָה֙ הַחוֹמָ֣ה אַחֶ֔רֶת וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק אֶת־הַמִּלּ֖וֹא עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּ֥עַשׂ שֶׁ֛לַח לָרֹ֖ב וּמָגִנִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he strengthened himself and built all the wall the broken down, and raised [it] on the towers, and outside [it] the wall another, and he strengthened the Millo [of the] city of David, and made weapon[s] in abundance and shields.

en.L: And he strengthened himself and built all the wall that was broken down, and raised [it] up on the towers, and outside [it] another wall; and he strengthened the Millo [in] the City of David, and made weapons in abundance, and shields.
en.B: Hezekiah took courage. He rebuilt all the wall where it was broken down and raised it up to the towers, and he built another wall outside it. He strengthened the Millo in the City of David and made large numbers of weapons and shields.
en.R: Hezekiah went to work with courage. He repaired every broken part of the city wall and built it up as high as the towers. He built a second wall outside the first one. He made the Millo (a supporting terrace) in the City of David stronger. He also made many weapons and shields.

decisions.choice: he strengthened himself: he took courage and acted with resolve
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of a king who sets himself firmly to a task (1:1; 15:8). It describes his resolve, which shows in the work that follows.

decisions.choice: raised [it] up on the towers: built the wall up to the height of its towers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "he raised on the towers", with no object. Read as it stands, the wall itself is raised to the towers. A small change to the text gives "he raised towers on it", which some early translations seem to reflect. Either way the walls were made higher and stronger.

decisions.choice: the Millo: a terrace or filled-in structure supporting buildings in the City of David
decisions.reason: The name comes from a word for filling. David and Solomon built it (1 Chronicles 11:8; 1 Kings 9:15); it was part of the defenses of the old city on the eastern hill.

decisions.choice: weapons: arms for throwing or thrusting, such as spears and javelins
decisions.reason: The word is used of weapons in general and of missiles. Together with shields it means Hezekiah equipped the defenders.

decisions.choice: the Millo (a supporting terrace)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, as 1 Kings 9:15 does.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֛ן שָׂרֵ֥י מִלְחָמ֖וֹת עַל־הָעָ֑ם וַיִּקְבְּצֵ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו אֶל־רְחוֹב֙ שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר עַל־לְבָבָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put commanders of wars over the people, and he gathered them to him to [the] square of [the] gate of the city, and he spoke to their heart, saying,

en.L: And he set commanders of war over the people, and he gathered them to himself at the square of the city gate, and he spoke to their heart, saying,
en.B: He appointed military commanders over the people and gathered them to him in the square at the city gate. Then he spoke encouragement to them:
en.R: He put army commanders in charge of the people. Then he called the people together in the open square by the city gate and encouraged them. He said,

decisions.choice: commanders of war over the people: officers set over the men of the city as fighters
decisions.reason: *'Am* here is the population of Jerusalem organized for its defense. *Sarim* in this military setting are commanders.

decisions.choice: the square of the city gate: the open space inside a gate, used for gatherings
decisions.reason: City gates had open areas where people met, trade was done and announcements made (Nehemiah 8:1).

decisions.choice: he spoke to their heart: he encouraged them
decisions.reason: To speak to someone's heart is to speak kindly so as to reassure or encourage (Genesis 50:21; Isaiah 40:2). Here it means strengthening their courage, as 30:22 uses it for words of encouragement.

source.text: חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ אַל־תִּֽירְא֣וּ וְאַל־תֵּחַ֗תּוּ מִפְּנֵי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וּמִלִּפְנֵ֖י כָּל־הֶהָמ֣וֹן אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־עִמָּ֥נוּ רַ֖ב מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Be strong and be bold; do not fear and do not be dismayed because of [the] king of Assyria and because of all the multitude which [is] with him, for with us [is] more than with him.

en.L: "Be strong and bold. Do not fear, and do not be dismayed because of the king of Assyria and because of all the multitude that [is] with him, for with us [is] more than with him.
en.B: "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and all the horde that is with him, for there is more on our side than on his.
en.R: "Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid. Do not lose heart because of the king of Assyria and the huge army with him. We have more on our side than he has.

decisions.choice: be strong and bold, do not fear or be dismayed: the words spoken to Joshua and to Israel before battle
decisions.reason: Hezekiah uses the charge Moses gave Israel and Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:6-8), which Yahweh repeated to Joshua (Joshua 1:9) and Joshua gave the army (Joshua 10:25). David used it for Solomon (1 Chronicles 22:13; 28:20). The king calls on the promise behind it, that Yahweh goes with his people.

decisions.choice: with us is more than with him: one greater, as verse 8 explains
alternatives: there are more with us than with him
decisions.reason: The word for "more" is singular and can mean "one greater". Verse 8 makes clear what Hezekiah means: Assyria has only human strength, while Judah has Yahweh. The saying recalls Elisha's words at Dothan (2 Kings 6:16).

decisions.choice: the multitude: a great, noisy crowd, here the Assyrian army
decisions.reason: The word suggests both size and noise, as the great army that came against Jehoshaphat (20:2, 12, 15).

decisions.choice: be strong and bold / be strong and courageous / be strong and brave
decisions.reason: The same wording as in Joshua at each level, so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: more on our side
decisions.reason: "Side" is supplied to make the comparison clear; "more" keeps the Hebrew's openness about whether it means numbers or power.

source.text: עִמּוֹ֙ זְר֣וֹעַ בָּשָׂ֔ר וְעִמָּ֜נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ לְעָזְרֵ֔נוּ וּלְהִלָּחֵ֖ם מִלְחֲמֹתֵ֑נוּ וַיִּסָּמְכ֣וּ הָעָ֔ם עַל־דִּבְרֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: With him [is] an arm of flesh, and with us [is] Yahweh our God to help us and to fight our battles. And leaned the people on [the] words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

en.L: With him [is] an arm of flesh, but with us [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people leaned on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
en.B: With him is only an arm of flesh, but we have {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God with us, to help us and fight our battles for us." And the people took confidence from the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
en.R: He has only human strength. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is with us. He will help us and fight our battles for us." The people were encouraged by what King Hezekiah of Judah told them.

decisions.choice: an arm of flesh: mere human strength
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength and "flesh" for what is human and weak, set against God. Jeremiah 17:5 uses the same picture of trusting in human power instead of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Yahweh our God, to help us and to fight our battles
decisions.reason: Hezekiah's confidence rests on Yahweh as the one who fights for his people, as at the Red Sea (Exodus 14:14) and in Jehoshaphat's day (20:15, 17).

decisions.choice: leaned on: relied on, took support from
decisions.reason: The verb means to lean or rest one's weight on something. The people's courage rested on what the king had told them.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: "Only" brings out the contrast the Hebrew makes by setting the two clauses side by side; Balanced and Readable also add "for us" to the battles.

decisions.choice: human strength
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the arm of flesh.

source.text: אַ֣חַר זֶ֗ה שָׁ֠לַח סַנְחֵרִ֨יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֤וּר עֲבָדָיו֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלַ֔יְמָה וְהוּא֙ עַל־לָכִ֔ישׁ וְכָל־מֶמְשַׁלְתּ֖וֹ עִמּ֑וֹ עַל־יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַל־כָּל־יְהוּדָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: After this sent Sennacherib king of Assyria his servants to Jerusalem, and he [was] at Lachish and all his dominion with him, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who [were] in Jerusalem, saying,

en.L: After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem, while he [was] at Lachish and all his forces with him, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who [were] in Jerusalem, saying,
en.B: After this, while Sennacherib king of Assyria was at Lachish with all his forces, he sent his officials to Jerusalem, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all the people of Judah who were in Jerusalem, with this message:
en.R: Later, King Sennacherib of Assyria was attacking the town of Lachish with his whole army. From there he sent his officials to Jerusalem with a message for King Hezekiah of Judah and for all the people of Judah who were in Jerusalem:

decisions.choice: Sennacherib's envoys from Lachish: 2 Kings 18:17
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 18:17 (and Isaiah 36:2) names three high officers and says they came with a large army and stood by the conduit of the Upper Pool. Chronicles calls them only "his servants" and does not name them or say where they stood.

decisions.choice: he was at Lachish: he was besieging Lachish
decisions.reason: "At" or "against" Lachish means he was laying siege to it. Lachish was the strongest town of Judah after Jerusalem, about thirty miles southwest of it.

decisions.choice: all his dominion: all his royal forces
decisions.reason: The word means rule or dominion; here, as in Jeremiah 34:1, it stands for the forces of his empire with him.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: *'Eved* used of a king's envoys is "servants" at Literal and "officials" at Balanced and Readable, as in 2 Kings 18-19.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֔ר סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר עַל־מָה֙ אַתֶּ֣ם בֹּטְחִ֔ים וְיֹשְׁבִ֥ים בְּמָצ֖וֹר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: on what [are] you trusting and remaining in siege in Jerusalem?

en.L: "Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: On what are you trusting, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
en.B: "Sennacherib king of Assyria says this: What are you relying on, that you stay in Jerusalem under siege?
en.R: "This is what King Sennacherib of Assyria says: Why do you feel so safe? What makes you stay in Jerusalem while it is surrounded?

decisions.choice: what are you trusting in?: the Rabshakeh's opening question, 2 Kings 18:19-20
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 18:19-20 (Isaiah 36:4-5) the speech opens with "What is this trust that you trust?" and "On whom do you rely?". Chronicles gives a shorter form of the same challenge and adds the siege.

decisions.choice: in siege: shut in under siege
decisions.reason: The word means siege, or a place under siege. The Assyrians present Jerusalem's people as already trapped. 2 Kings does not say Jerusalem was formally besieged, and the word may describe the threat as much as an army already dug in around the walls.

decisions.choice: Thus says / ... says this / This is what ... says
decisions.reason: The messenger formula has the same wording as in 2 Kings 18:19 at each level.

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: Readable splits the one question into two short ones.

source.text: הֲלֹ֤א יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מַסִּ֣ית אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָתֵ֣ת אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָמ֛וּת בְּרָעָ֥ב וּבְצָמָ֖א לֵאמֹ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ יַצִּילֵ֕נוּ מִכַּ֖ף מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not Hezekiah misleading you to give you to die by hunger and by thirst, saying, Yahweh our God will deliver us from [the] palm of [the] king of Assyria?

en.L: Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die by famine and by thirst, saying, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God will deliver us from the palm of the king of Assyria'?
en.B: Is Hezekiah not misleading you, handing you over to die of hunger and thirst, when he says, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God will rescue us from the power of the king of Assyria'?
en.R: Hezekiah is fooling you. He says, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God will save us from the king of Assyria.' But he is leading you to die of hunger and thirst.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah misleads you, saying Yahweh will deliver us: 2 Kings 18:30, 32
decisions.reason: The same charge as in 2 Kings 18:30, 32, with the same verb for "mislead". Chronicles adds that by holding out, the people will die of hunger and thirst, which 2 Kings 18:27 says more coarsely.

decisions.choice: from the palm of: from the power of
decisions.reason: "Palm" or "hand" stands for grip and control.

decisions.choice: is not Hezekiah ...?: a question expecting the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question is an accusation.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: Readable states the accusation outright and puts Hezekiah's words before the result.

source.text: הֲלֹא־הוּא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ הֵסִ֥יר אֶת־בָּמֹתָ֖יו וְאֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתָ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה וְלִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לִפְנֵ֨י מִזְבֵּ֧חַ אֶחָ֛ד תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ וְעָלָ֥יו תַּקְטִֽירוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not he, Hezekiah, [who] removed his high places and his altars, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, saying, before altar one you will bow down and on it you will make smoke?

en.L: Did not this Hezekiah remove {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} high places and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} altars, and say to Judah and to Jerusalem, 'Before one altar you shall bow down, and on it you shall make [offerings] smoke'?
en.B: Did this same Hezekiah not get rid of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} high places and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} altars and tell Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must bow down before one altar and burn your offerings on it'?
en.R: Hezekiah himself tore down {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hilltop shrines and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} altars. He told the people of Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship at only one altar and burn your offerings only on it.'

decisions.choice: Hezekiah removed his high places and altars: 2 Kings 18:22
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 18:22 (Isaiah 36:7) the officer's "he" is Yahweh, whose high places Hezekiah removed. Here "he, Hezekiah" points to the king, and "his" to Yahweh named in verse 11. Kings has "before this altar ... in Jerusalem"; Chronicles says "one altar", stressing that only one place of worship was left.

decisions.choice: the Assyrian misreads Hezekiah's reform
decisions.reason: To the Assyrian, closing the shrines looks like an insult to Israel's God. For the writer it was faithfulness (31:1), which makes the taunt ironic.

decisions.choice: make smoke: burn offerings, whether incense or sacrifices
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke on an altar, and is used of incense and of sacrificial portions alike.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: *Bamot* is "hilltop shrines" at Readable, as in Kings; Readable names Yahweh for the first "his".

decisions.choice: [offerings] / your offerings
decisions.reason: The object of the verb is supplied.

source.text: הֲלֹ֣א תֵדְע֗וּ מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י וַאֲבוֹתַ֔י לְכֹ֖ל עַמֵּ֣י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת הֲיָכ֣וֹל יָֽכְל֗וּ אֱלֹהֵי֙ גּוֹיֵ֣ הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: [Do] not you know what have done I and my fathers to all [the] peoples of the lands? Were at all able [the] gods of [the] nations of the lands to deliver their land from my hand?

en.L: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands at all able to deliver their land from my hand?
en.B: Do you not know what I and my forefathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of the nations in those lands ever able to rescue their land from my hand?
en.R: You know what I and the kings before me have done to the peoples of all the other lands. Were the gods of those nations able to save their land from me? Not at all!

decisions.choice: the gods of the nations could not deliver their land: 2 Kings 18:33-35; 19:11-12
decisions.reason: The boast gathers what the officer said in 2 Kings 18:33-35 and the letter in 19:11-12. Chronicles leaves out the list of cities (Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim and others) and keeps the argument.

decisions.choice: were they at all able?: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: Repeating the verb sharpens the question, which expects the answer no.

decisions.choice: my fathers: the Assyrian kings before me
decisions.reason: Sennacherib counts the conquests of earlier kings of Assyria as his own line's record.

decisions.choice: a statement, and an added answer
decisions.reason: Readable turns the first question into a statement and spells out the answer the second expects.

source.text: מִ֠י בְּֽכָל־אֱלֹהֵ֞י הַגּוֹיִ֤ם הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱרִ֣ימוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָכ֔וֹל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִ֑י כִּ֤י יוּכַל֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Who among all [the] gods of the nations the these which devoted to destruction my fathers [is there] who was able to deliver his people from my hand, that should be able your God to deliver you from my hand?

en.L: Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers devoted to destruction [was there] who was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?
en.B: Which of all the gods of these nations that my forefathers devoted to destruction was able to rescue its people from my hand? How then could your God rescue you from my hand?
en.R: My ancestors completely destroyed these nations, and not one of their gods could save its people from me. So how could your God save you from me?

decisions.choice: who among all the gods ...?: 2 Kings 18:35
decisions.reason: The question follows 2 Kings 18:35 (Isaiah 36:20), "Who among all the gods of the lands ...?". Chronicles says "nations" for "lands" and adds that his fathers devoted them to destruction.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction: destroyed completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for *cherem*, total destruction. In the Assyrian's mouth it is a boast of conquest that left nothing standing.

decisions.choice: your God: the Assyrian puts Israel's God on a level with the others
decisions.reason: Sennacherib treats Yahweh as one more national god. The writer answers this in verse 19 and in what follows.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable split the long question; Readable states the first part as fact.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה אַל־יַשִּׁיא֩ אֶתְכֶ֨ם חִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וְאַל־יַסִּ֨ית אֶתְכֶ֣ם כָּזֹאת֮ וְאַל־תַּאֲמִ֣ינוּ לוֹ֒ כִּי־לֹ֣א יוּכַ֗ל כָּל־אֱל֨וֹהַ֙ כָּל־גּ֣וֹי וּמַמְלָכָ֔ה לְהַצִּ֥יל עַמּ֛וֹ מִיָּדִ֖י וּמִיַּ֣ד אֲבוֹתָ֑י אַ֚ף כִּ֣י אֱֽלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם לֹא־יַצִּ֥ילוּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, let not deceive you Hezekiah, and let him not mislead you like this, and do not believe him; for not has been able any god of any nation and kingdom to deliver his people from my hand and from [the] hand of my fathers. How much less your God will deliver you from my hand!

en.L: And now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you, and do not let him mislead you like this, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you from my hand!"
en.B: So now, do not let Hezekiah fool you or mislead you like this. Do not believe him. No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue its people from my hand or from the hand of my forefathers. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand!"
en.R: So do not let Hezekiah trick you or lead you astray like this. Do not believe him! No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to save its people from me or from the kings before me. Your God certainly cannot save you from me!"

decisions.choice: do not let Hezekiah deceive you: 2 Kings 18:29
decisions.reason: The same verb for "deceive" as in 2 Kings 18:29 (Isaiah 36:14); Chronicles adds "mislead" from 2 Kings 18:32 and "do not believe him".

decisions.choice: how much less your God: an argument from the greater to the lesser
decisions.reason: If no god of any nation could save its people, the Assyrian argues, Judah's God can do even less. The verb with "your God" is plural, as if the speaker thought of Israel's God as one more set of gods (compare verse 19).

decisions.choice: any god: the singular word for a god
decisions.reason: The Assyrian uses the less common singular word for a god, making his claim cover each god one by one.

decisions.choice: fool (Balanced); trick (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 18:29 at the same levels.

source.text: וְעוֹד֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ עֲבָדָ֔יו עַל־יְהוָ֖ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And still spoke his servants against Yahweh the God and against Hezekiah his servant.

en.L: And his servants spoke still more against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God and against Hezekiah {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave.
en.B: His officials said still more against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God and against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Hezekiah.
en.R: Sennacherib's officials said even more things against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God and against Hezekiah, who served {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: still more: the writer cuts the speeches short
decisions.reason: The writer gives only a sample of what was said (compare 2 Kings 18:19-35) and sums up the rest.

decisions.choice: his servants ... his servant: Sennacherib's officials against Yahweh's servant
decisions.reason: The same word names the Assyrian king's officials and Hezekiah as Yahweh's servant, setting the two masters side by side.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *'Eved* for Hezekiah as Yahweh's servant follows the rule for "my servant David"; for Sennacherib's envoys it is "servants" at Literal and "officials" at the other levels.

source.text: וּסְפָרִ֣ים כָּתַ֔ב לְחָרֵ֕ף לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֵֽאמֹ֨ר עָלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֵּֽאלֹהֵ֞י גּוֹיֵ֤ הָאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־הִצִּ֤ילוּ עַמָּם֙ מִיָּדִ֔י כֵּ֣ן לֹֽא־יַצִּ֞יל אֱלֹהֵ֧י יְחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And letters he wrote to taunt Yahweh God of Israel and to say against him, saying, like [the] gods of [the] nations of the lands which not delivered their people from my hand, so not will deliver [the] God of Hezekiah his people from my hand.

en.L: And he wrote letters to taunt {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel and to speak against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Like the gods of the nations of the lands, which have not delivered their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from my hand."
en.B: He also wrote letters to insult {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, and to speak against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Just as the gods of the nations of other lands have not rescued their people from my hand, so Hezekiah's God will not rescue {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from my hand."
en.R: Sennacherib also wrote letters that insulted {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. He wrote this against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "The gods of the other nations could not save their people from me. In the same way, Hezekiah's God will not save {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from me."

decisions.choice: he wrote letters: 2 Kings 19:9-14
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 19:9-14 (Isaiah 37:9-14) tells of a second message, which Hezekiah received as letters and spread out before Yahweh. Chronicles mentions the letters but not Hezekiah's taking them into the temple.

decisions.choice: taunt: heap scorn on, insult
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 2 Kings 19:4, 16 of the Assyrian sending his officer "to taunt the living God".

decisions.choice: the God of Hezekiah: as if Yahweh were one king's private god
decisions.reason: Sennacherib names Israel's God by the king who worships him, making him small, one god among many.

decisions.choice: insult
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 19:4, 16 at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ בְקוֹל־גָּד֜וֹל יְהוּדִ֗ית עַל־עַ֤ם יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה לְיָֽרְאָ֖ם וּֽלְבַהֲלָ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן יִלְכְּד֥וּ אֶת־הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they called with a voice great [in] Judean to [the] people of Jerusalem who [were] on the wall, to make them afraid and to terrify them, so that they might capture the city.

en.L: And they called out with a loud voice [in] Judean to the people of Jerusalem who [were] on the wall, to make them afraid and to terrify them, so that they might capture the city.
en.B: They shouted in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem on the wall, trying to frighten and terrify them so that they could take the city.
en.R: The officials shouted loudly in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem standing on the city wall. They wanted to frighten them and fill them with terror so that they could capture the city.

decisions.choice: shouting in Judean to the people on the wall: 2 Kings 18:26-28
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 18:26-28 Hezekiah's officers ask the Assyrian to speak in Aramaic, not in the language of Judah, for the people on the wall to hear; he refuses and shouts louder. Chronicles keeps only the shouting and its aim.

decisions.choice: Judean: the Hebrew spoken in Judah
decisions.reason: The word names the language of the kingdom of Judah, set against Aramaic, the language of diplomacy (2 Kings 18:26).

decisions.choice: to frighten them so as to take the city
decisions.reason: The writer makes the Assyrians' aim plain: the speeches were a weapon, meant to break the city's will without a fight.

decisions.choice: in Hebrew
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 18:28 at Readable.

source.text: וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כְּעַ֗ל אֱלֹהֵי֙ עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they spoke of [the] God of Jerusalem as of [the] gods of [the] peoples of the earth, [the] work of [the] hands of the man.

en.L: And they spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of the hands of man.
en.B: They spoke about the God of Jerusalem as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were one of the gods of the earth's peoples, the work of human hands.
en.R: They talked about the God of Jerusalem as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were like the gods of the other peoples of the world. Those gods are only things that people have made with their hands.

decisions.choice: the God of Jerusalem treated as a man-made god
decisions.reason: This is the writer's verdict on the whole Assyrian speech: they put the living God on a level with idols. The phrase "the work of human hands" is the Bible's standing description of idols (Deuteronomy 4:28; 2 Kings 19:18; Psalm 115:4).

decisions.choice: the work of human hands: 2 Kings 19:18
decisions.reason: In Hezekiah's prayer in 2 Kings 19:18 (Isaiah 37:19) the gods of the nations were "no gods, but the work of human hands", which is why Assyria could destroy them. Chronicles gives the thought to the narrator instead of the prayer.

decisions.choice: man: humankind
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: human hands; people
decisions.reason: The word means humankind, so Balanced and Readable say "human" and "people".

source.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֞ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וִֽישַֽׁעְיָ֧הוּ בֶן־אָמ֛וֹץ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל־זֹ֑את וַֽיִּזְעֲק֖וּ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And prayed Hezekiah the king and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet about this, and they cried out [to] the heavens.

en.L: And Hezekiah the king and Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, prayed about this, and they cried out [to] heaven.
en.B: Then King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed about this and cried out to heaven.
en.R: So King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed about this. They cried out to God in heaven.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah and Isaiah pray: 2 Kings 19:1-4, 14-20
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 19 Hezekiah sends to Isaiah asking him to pray (19:4), then prays himself in the temple (19:15-19), and Isaiah sends Yahweh's answer (19:20-34). Chronicles sums this up as both men praying together and leaves out Isaiah's oracle.

decisions.choice: cried out to heaven: cried out to God
decisions.reason: "Heaven" stands for God who lives there, a way of speaking found often in Chronicles and later books (compare 2 Chronicles 6:21).

decisions.choice: to God in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom "heaven" stands for.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ מַלְאָ֔ךְ וַיַּכְחֵ֞ד כָּל־גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֨יִל֙ וְנָגִ֣יד וְשָׂ֔ר בְּמַחֲנֵ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּשָׁב֩ בְּבֹ֨שֶׁת פָּנִ֜ים לְאַרְצ֗וֹ וַיָּבֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהָ֔יו וּמִֽיצִיאֵ֣י מֵעָ֔יו שָׁ֖ם הִפִּילֻ֥הוּ בֶחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Yahweh an angel, and he cut off every mighty man of valor and leader and commander in [the] camp of [the] king of Assyria. And he returned with shame of face to his land, and he came [into the] house of his god, and some of [those] coming out of his inner parts there struck him down with the sword.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent an angel, and he cut off every mighty man of valor and ruler and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. And he returned with shame of face to his own land. And he came [into] the house of his god, and some of those who came out of his own body struck him down there with the sword.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent an angel, who cut off every mighty warrior, ruler and commander in the Assyrian king's camp. Sennacherib went back to his own land in disgrace. And when he went into the house of his god, some of his own offspring cut him down there with the sword.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent an angel who destroyed all the brave warriors, leaders and commanders in the Assyrian king's camp. So Sennacherib went back to his own country, deeply ashamed. Later he went into the temple of his god, and some of his own sons killed him there with a sword.

decisions.choice: the angel strikes the Assyrian camp: 2 Kings 19:35-37
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 19:35-37 (Isaiah 37:36-38) tells of the angel of Yahweh striking 185,000 in one night, names the god Nisroch, the sons Adrammelech and Sharezer, and the new king Esarhaddon. Chronicles gives no number or names and stresses that the army's leaders were cut off.

decisions.choice: with shame of face: in disgrace
decisions.reason: Shame is pictured on the face, the opposite of the bold face he showed in verse 2.

decisions.choice: those who came out of his own body: his own sons
decisions.reason: "Inner parts" stands for the body as the source of children (Genesis 15:4; 2 Samuel 7:12). The phrase stresses the irony: his own god's house could not protect him, and his own sons killed him. 2 Kings 19:37 names two of them.

decisions.choice: he went into the house of his god: an Assyrian temple
decisions.reason: According to 2 Kings 19:37 this was the temple of Nisroch in Nineveh. The murder happened about twenty years after the campaign; the writer joins the two because one explains the other.

decisions.choice: his own offspring
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress on his own children without naming the picture; Readable says "sons", as 2 Kings 19:37.

decisions.choice: Sennacherib
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king, since the subject changes from the angel.

source.text: וַיּוֹשַׁע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וְאֵ֣ת׀יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם מִיַּ֛ד סַנְחֵרִ֥יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֖וּר וּמִיַּד־כֹּ֑ל וַֽיְנַהֲלֵ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And saved Yahweh Hezekiah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem from [the] hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from [the] hand of all, and he guided them from around.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all [others], and he guided them on every side.
en.B: In this way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the power of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the power of everyone else, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took care of them on every side.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from King Sennacherib of Assyria and from all their other enemies. He watched over them on every side.

decisions.choice: he guided them on every side: he cared for them like a shepherd
alternatives: he gave them rest on every side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb means to lead or guide, as a shepherd leads a flock to water (Psalm 23:2; Isaiah 40:11). Some early translations read a slightly different text, "he gave them rest on every side", a phrase Chronicles uses elsewhere (14:6; 15:15; 20:30).

decisions.choice: from the hand of all: from every enemy
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power; "all" means all others who threatened them.

decisions.choice: Yahweh saved: the answer to Hezekiah's words in verses 7-8
decisions.reason: What the king promised, that Yahweh would help and fight for them, has come true.

source.text: וְ֠רַבִּים מְבִיאִ֨ים מִנְחָ֤ה לַיהוָה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּמִ֨גְדָּנ֔וֹת לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנַּשֵּׂ֛א לְעֵינֵ֥י כָל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם מֵאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And many [were] bringing an offering to Yahweh to Jerusalem and choice gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah, and he was lifted up in [the] eyes of all the nations from after this.

en.L: And many were bringing an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to Jerusalem, and choice gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah, and he was lifted up in the eyes of all the nations from then on.
en.B: Many brought gifts to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem and costly presents to Hezekiah king of Judah, and from then on he was highly regarded by all the nations.
en.R: Many people brought gifts to Jerusalem for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and valuable presents for King Hezekiah of Judah. From then on, all the nations respected him greatly.

decisions.choice: an offering: a gift brought in honor, here to Yahweh
decisions.reason: *Minchah* is a gift or tribute, and in worship a grain offering. Here it is gifts from outsiders honoring the God who had saved Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: choice gifts: costly, precious things
decisions.reason: The word is used of valuable gifts (Genesis 24:53).

decisions.choice: lifted up in the eyes of: highly regarded by
decisions.reason: To be lifted up in someone's eyes is to be honored by them. The nations that had heard Assyria's boasts now honored the God and king it had threatened.

source.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ עַד־לָמ֑וּת וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ וּמוֹפֵ֖ת נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: In the days those became sick Hezekiah to die, and he prayed to Yahweh, and he spoke to him and a sign he gave to him.

en.L: In those days Hezekiah became sick to [the point of] dying, and he prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to him and gave him a sign.
en.B: In those days Hezekiah fell ill and was close to death. He prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who answered him and gave him a sign.
en.R: Around that time Hezekiah became so sick that he was about to die. He prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him and gave him a sign.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah's illness and the sign: 2 Kings 20:1-11
decisions.reason: The opening matches 2 Kings 20:1 (Isaiah 38:1) word for word. Chronicles then sums up in a few words what 2 Kings 20:1-11 tells at length: Isaiah's message, Hezekiah's prayer and tears, the promise of fifteen more years, and the shadow going back on the steps of Ahaz.

decisions.choice: he spoke to him: Yahweh answered Hezekiah
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it is most naturally Yahweh, to whom Hezekiah prayed, who answered through Isaiah (2 Kings 20:4-6).

decisions.choice: a sign: a wonder given as proof
decisions.reason: The word means a sign or wonder, here the shadow turned back (2 Kings 20:8-11). Verse 31 calls it "the sign that had happened in the land".

decisions.choice: answered
decisions.reason: "Spoke to him" in reply to prayer is put as "answered".

source.text: וְלֹא־כִגְמֻ֤ל עָלָיו֙ הֵשִׁ֣יב יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ וַיְהִ֤י עָלָיו֙ קֶ֔צֶף וְעַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And not according to [the] benefit [done] to him did return Hezekiah, for was high his heart; and there was on him wrath, and on Judah and Jerusalem.

en.L: But Hezekiah did not return according to the benefit [done] to him, for his heart was high; and there was wrath on him and on Judah and Jerusalem.
en.B: But Hezekiah did not respond in keeping with the kindness shown to him, because his heart became proud. So wrath came on him and on Judah and Jerusalem.
en.R: But Hezekiah did not show thanks for the good that had been done for him. He became proud. So God was angry with him and with Judah and Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: did not return according to the benefit: did not repay the kindness he had received
decisions.reason: The noun means what is done to someone, here the good Yahweh had done in healing him. To "return" it is to answer it fittingly, with gratitude and humility.

decisions.choice: his heart was high: he became proud
decisions.reason: A "high" heart is pride, as with Uzziah (26:16). The writer may be thinking of the Babylonian visit, where Hezekiah showed off his wealth (verse 31; 2 Kings 20:13).

decisions.choice: wrath: God's anger, which brings judgment
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses this word for Yahweh's anger against sin (19:2, 10; 24:18). It fell on the people as well as the king.

decisions.choice: God was angry
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one whose wrath it was, as verse 26 says.

source.text: וַיִּכָּנַ֤ע יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ ה֖וּא וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־בָ֤א עֲלֵיהֶם֙ קֶ֣צֶף יְהוָ֔ה בִּימֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And humbled himself Hezekiah in [the] pride of his heart, he and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, and not came on them [the] wrath of Yahweh in [the] days of Hezekiah.

en.L: And Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not come on them in the days of Hezekiah.
en.B: Then Hezekiah humbled himself for his proud heart, he and the people of Jerusalem with him, so the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not come on them in Hezekiah's days.
en.R: But then Hezekiah turned from his pride and humbled himself, and so did the people of Jerusalem. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not punish them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger while Hezekiah was alive.

decisions.choice: in the pride of his heart: he humbled himself from his pride
decisions.reason: The phrase names what he humbled himself over: he turned from the pride of verse 25.

decisions.choice: humbled himself: the turning that Chronicles says Yahweh answers
decisions.reason: Yahweh had promised to hear those who humble themselves (7:14), as with Rehoboam (12:6-7, 12).

decisions.choice: not in the days of Hezekiah: 2 Kings 20:16-19
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 20:16-19 (Isaiah 39:5-8) Isaiah announces that all Hezekiah's treasures will be carried to Babylon, but not in his lifetime, and Hezekiah accepts it. Chronicles says the judgment was held back because he humbled himself.

decisions.choice: did not punish them in his anger
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the wrath did not come" as an action of Yahweh.

source.text: וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְאֹֽצָר֣וֹת עָֽשָׂה־ל֠וֹ לְכֶ֨סֶף וּלְזָהָ֜ב וּלְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֗ה וְלִבְשָׂמִים֙ וּלְמָ֣גִנִּ֔ים וּלְכֹ֖ל כְּלֵ֥י חֶמְדָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And there was to Hezekiah riches and honor much very; and treasuries he made for himself for silver and for gold and for stone precious and for spices and for shields and for all [the] vessels of desire,

en.L: And Hezekiah had very much riches and honor; and he made for himself treasuries for silver and for gold and for precious stones and for spices and for shields and for all [kinds of] desirable vessels,
en.B: Hezekiah had very great wealth and honor. He made himself treasuries for silver and gold, for precious stones and spices, for shields and for all kinds of valuable things,
en.R: Hezekiah was very rich and highly honored. He built storerooms for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices and shields, and for all kinds of valuable things.

decisions.choice: riches and honor: the sign of God's blessing, as with David, Solomon and Jehoshaphat
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses the same pair for David (1 Chronicles 29:28), Solomon (1:12) and Jehoshaphat (17:5; 18:1). Verse 29 gives the reason: God had given it.

decisions.choice: shields: probably ornamental shields of precious metal
decisions.reason: Listed among treasures, these were likely display shields like Solomon's shields of gold (9:15-16), kept as stored wealth.

decisions.choice: vessels of desire: costly objects of every kind
decisions.reason: "Vessels" covers all kinds of articles; "of desire" means precious.

source.text: וּמִ֨סְכְּנ֔וֹת לִתְבוּאַ֥ת דָּגָ֖ן וְתִיר֣וֹשׁ וְיִצְהָ֑ר וְאֻֽרָוֺת֙ לְכָל־בְּהֵמָ֣ה וּבְהֵמָ֔ה וַעֲדָרִ֖ים לָאֲוֵרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: and storehouses for [the] produce of grain and new wine and oil, and stalls for all [kinds of] beast and beast, and flocks for folds.

en.L: and storehouses for the produce of grain and new wine and oil, and stalls for all [kinds of] livestock and livestock, and flocks for folds.
en.B: and storehouses for the harvest of grain, new wine and oil. He also made stalls for every kind of livestock and folds for the flocks.
en.R: He also built storehouses for grain, new wine and olive oil. He built stalls for all kinds of cattle and pens for his flocks.

decisions.choice: all beast and beast: every kind of livestock
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun means "of every kind".

decisions.choice: flocks for folds: folds for the flocks
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "flocks for the folds". The sense is that he had pens made for his flocks; the order of the words may be a way of saying the folds were filled with flocks.

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and oil: the three main crops of the land
decisions.reason: The same three are the land's staple harvest throughout the Bible (Deuteronomy 7:13; 2 Chronicles 31:5).

decisions.choice: livestock and livestock
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated noun; the other levels say "every kind".

source.text: וְעָרִים֙ עָ֣שָׂה ל֔וֹ וּמִקְנֵה־צֹ֥אן וּבָקָ֖ר לָרֹ֑ב כִּ֤י נָֽתַן־לוֹ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים רְכ֖וּשׁ רַ֥ב מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And cities he made for himself, and possessions of flock and herd in abundance, for gave to him God property great very.

en.L: And he made cities for himself, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance, for God gave him very great property.
en.B: He also built towns for himself and acquired great numbers of flocks and herds, for God had given him very great wealth.
en.R: He built towns and owned large flocks of sheep and goats and herds of cattle, because God had made him very rich.

decisions.choice: cities: towns he built or fortified
decisions.reason: The text reads "cities". Because the list is about livestock, some have suggested a word of almost the same letters meaning "donkeys", but no manuscript reads so.

decisions.choice: for God gave him: his wealth was God's gift
decisions.reason: The writer ties Hezekiah's prosperity to God's blessing on his faithfulness (31:21).

decisions.choice: flock and herd: sheep and goats, and cattle
decisions.reason: *Tso'n* covers sheep and goats; *baqar* is cattle.

source.text: וְה֣וּא יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ סָתַם֙ אֶת־מוֹצָ֞א מֵימֵ֤י גִיחוֹן֙ הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן וַֽיַּישְּׁרֵ֥ם לְמַֽטָּה־מַּעְרָ֖בָה לְעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּצְלַ֥ח יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכָֽל־מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he, Hezekiah, stopped up [the] outlet of [the] waters of Gihon the upper, and directed them down to west to [the] city of David. And prospered Hezekiah in all his work.

en.L: And he, Hezekiah, stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them straight down to the west of the City of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his work.
en.B: It was Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and channeled them straight down to the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah succeeded in everything he did.
en.R: Hezekiah was the one who blocked the upper outlet of the Gihon spring. He made its water flow down through a tunnel to the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah was successful in everything he did.

decisions.choice: the Gihon water brought into the city: 2 Kings 20:20
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 20:20 mentions how Hezekiah "made the pool and the conduit and brought the water into the city". Chronicles says where the water came from and where it went.

decisions.choice: the upper outlet of Gihon: Jerusalem's spring, cut off outside and led inside the walls
decisions.reason: The Gihon spring rises in the Kidron Valley, east of the City of David and outside its wall. A tunnel more than five hundred yards long, cut through the rock and found in 1880 with an inscription telling how it was dug, carries its water to the Pool of Siloam on the west side of the old city. It is generally identified as Hezekiah's work.

decisions.choice: directed them straight: led them in a straight course
decisions.reason: The verb means to make straight or level, here to guide the water's course.

decisions.choice: through a tunnel
decisions.reason: Readable names the means, which 2 Kings 20:20 calls a conduit; the tunnel is still there.

decisions.choice: It was Hezekiah who
decisions.reason: The added "he" puts weight on Hezekiah; Balanced gives that stress.

source.text: וְכֵ֞ן בִּמְלִיצֵ֣י׀שָׂרֵ֣י בָּבֶ֗ל הַֽמְשַׁלְּחִ֤ים עָלָיו֙ לִדְרֹ֗שׁ הַמּוֹפֵת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה בָאָ֔רֶץ עֲזָב֖וֹ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים לְנַ֨סּוֹת֔וֹ לָדַ֖עַת כָּל־בִּלְבָבֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And so in [the matter of the] envoys of [the] princes of Babylon the [ones] sent to him to inquire [about] the sign that had been in the land, left him God to test him, to know all [that was] in his heart.

en.L: And so, in [the matter of] the envoys of the princes of Babylon, who were sent to him to inquire about the sign that had happened in the land, God left him, to test him, to know all [that was] in his heart.
en.B: And so, in the matter of the envoys of the officials of Babylon who were sent to him to ask about the sign that had happened in the land, God left him to himself to test him, to know everything that was in his heart.
en.R: Then the leaders of Babylon sent messengers to Hezekiah to ask about the miracle that had happened in the land. At that time God left Hezekiah on his own. God did this to test him and to show everything that was in his heart.

decisions.choice: the Babylonian envoys: 2 Kings 20:12-19
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 20:12-19 (Isaiah 39) tells how Berodach-baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift, how Hezekiah showed the envoys all his treasures, and how Isaiah rebuked him. Chronicles gives a different purpose for the visit, to ask about the sign, and tells what God was doing in it.

decisions.choice: envoys: spokesmen, go-betweens
decisions.reason: The word means interpreters or spokesmen, people who speak for another (Genesis 42:23).

decisions.choice: God left him to test him, to know all that was in his heart: Deuteronomy 8:2
decisions.reason: Moses said that Yahweh led Israel through the wilderness "to test you, to know what was in your heart". God's testing brings into the open what a person truly is; it is not that God lacked the knowledge.

decisions.choice: and so: even so, in the case of
decisions.reason: The phrase links the visit with what has just been said of Hezekiah's success and pride. It may also be read "but even so", marking the visit as the one exception to his success.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders
decisions.reason: *Sar* follows the usual table.

decisions.choice: miracle
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of sign it was.

source.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ וַחֲסָדָ֑יו הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים בַּחֲז֞וֹן יְשַֽׁעְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־אָמוֹץ֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא עַל־סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵי־יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Hezekiah and his loyal deeds, look, they [are] written in [the] vision of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet, on [the] book of [the] kings of Judah and Israel.

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Hezekiah, and his faithful deeds, look, they [are] written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
en.B: The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his faithful deeds are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
en.R: Everything else Hezekiah did, including the faithful things he did, is written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

decisions.choice: the sources formula, in Chronicles' form; parallel to 2 Kings 20:20
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 20:20 points to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah" and names his might and the water tunnel. Chronicles names his faithful deeds and adds the vision of Isaiah.

decisions.choice: his faithful deeds: acts of loyalty to God
decisions.reason: The plural of *chesed*, the word for steadfast loyalty, here names Hezekiah's faithful acts for God's house and worship (as of Josiah, 35:26; Nehemiah 13:14).

decisions.choice: the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz: Isaiah's prophecies
decisions.reason: Isaiah's book opens "The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz" (Isaiah 1:1), and chapters 36-39 tell these events.

decisions.choice: in the book of the kings: Isaiah's vision as part of the book, or a second source
alternatives: and in the book of the kings
decisions.reason: The vision may be described as found within the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel, or the two may be named as separate sources.

decisions.choice: faithful deeds (Literal, Balanced); faithful things he did (Readable)
decisions.reason: The usual "steadfast love" or "faithful love" fits God's love better than a list of a king's deeds, so these words name the deeds. The same wording is used for Josiah at 35:26.

decisions.choice: "look" left out; the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel (Balanced); the book of the kings of Judah and Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 16:11 and 27:7.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻהוּ֮ בְּֽמַעֲלֵה֮ קִבְרֵ֣י בְנֵי־דָוִיד֒ וְכָבוֹד֙ עָֽשׂוּ־ל֣וֹ בְמוֹת֔וֹ כָּל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Hezekiah with his fathers, and they buried him in [the] ascent of [the] tombs of [the] sons of David, and honor they did to him at his death, all Judah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem. And reigned Manasseh his son in his place.

en.L: And Hezekiah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honor at his death. And Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Then Hezekiah rested with his ancestors, and they buried him on the ascent to the tombs of David's descendants. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him at his death. His son Manasseh became king in his place.
en.R: Then Hezekiah died and was buried on the slope where the tombs of David's descendants are. All the people of Judah and Jerusalem honored him when he died. His son Manasseh became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The usual way the books of Kings and Chronicles speak of a king's death.

decisions.choice: the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David: a place of honor among the royal tombs
alternatives: the upper part of the tombs
decisions.reason: *Ma'aleh* is a slope or rise, and may mean the upper part of the burial ground. Either way the burial place itself honored him.

decisions.choice: honor at his death; Manasseh reigned: 2 Kings 20:21
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 20:21 says only that he lay down with his fathers and Manasseh reigned. Chronicles adds the burial and the honor the people gave him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula, worded as in 2 Kings 20:21 and 2 Chronicles 27:9.
